extName.message: crxdiff: what changed in your extensions

extDescription.message: Shows what each update to your extensions changed: new permissions, new sites, risky code. Nothing leaves your device.

actionTitle.message: crxdiff: what changed in your extensions

level_high_hint.message: This update made changes that malicious updates often make. Review it before you keep using the extension.

level_medium_hint.message: This update gives the extension more reach. That is often fine; check that it fits what the extension does.

level_low_hint.message: Small changes that are rarely a problem on their own.

level_none_hint.message: The code changed, but nothing on crxdiff’s watch list did.

popup_empty_body.message: crxdiff saved a baseline of each extension. When one updates, you will see here what changed.

report_why_none.message: Nothing on the watch list changed.

report_scale.message: 20 points or more is “worth a look”, 50 or more is “high risk”.

report_access_none.message: No change to permissions or site access.

report_sites_help.message: Hosts in full URLs inside the extension’s scripts and pages that were not there before. A name in the code does not prove the extension connects to it.

report_code_none.message: No risky pattern appeared for the first time.

report_reenable_failed.message: Chrome did not allow turning it back on: {1}

ov_reports_none.message: No reports yet. crxdiff writes one each time a watched extension updates.

status_baseline_ahead_help.message: The store already serves {1}; you have {2}. When Chrome installs {1}, that update will show permission changes only.

status_baseline_behind_help.message: The store serves {1}, older than your {2}. crxdiff will try again later.

status_error_help.message: Error: {1}. crxdiff will try again on the next check.

status_unavailable_help.message: The Chrome Web Store no longer serves this extension. Extensions are sometimes removed for breaking store policy.

r_not_extension.message: Apps and themes are not checked.

r_unpacked.message: Loaded unpacked (developer mode), so there is no store version to compare.

r_edge_store.message: From the Microsoft Edge store. Only the Chrome Web Store is supported for now.

r_self_hosted.message: Updates from its own server ({1}), not from the Chrome Web Store.

r_sideload.message: Installed by another program on this computer.

r_other.message: Installed in a way crxdiff cannot check.

n_store_ahead.message: The store already serves {1}, newer than the {2} you have. This report describes {1}, which Chrome will install soon.

n_no_old_package.message: crxdiff had no package for {1}, so only the permission changes Chrome reports are shown.

n_store_behind.message: The store serves {1}, older than the installed {2}, so only permission changes are shown.

n_auto_disabled.message: crxdiff turned this extension off because the update is high risk and automatic turn-off is on in Settings.

n_auto_disable_failed.message: Automatic turn-off is on, but Chrome does not allow turning this extension off.

f_perm_added_silent_why.message: Chrome shows no prompt for this permission, so the update installed without asking you.

f_perm_added_warn_why.message: Chrome warns about this one and keeps the extension off until you accept it.

f_perm_added_unknown_why.message: crxdiff does not know this permission yet.

f_host_added_broad.message: Can now read and change all sites ({1})

f_host_added_broad_why.message: Access to every site lets the extension see and change any page, including sign-in pages and forms.

f_host_added_why.message: The extension can now read and change these sites.

f_optional_added_why.message: The extension may ask you for these later.

f_match_added_broad.message: Now runs a script on every page ({1})

f_match_added_broad_why.message: A content script on all pages can read what you see and type on any site.

f_match_added_why.message: Its content scripts now also run on these pages.

f_main_world.message: A content script now runs inside the page itself

f_main_world_why.message: Scripts in the “MAIN” world share the page’s JavaScript instead of running isolated from it.

f_csp_unsafe_eval_why.message: “unsafe-eval” lets the extension turn text into code while it runs, a common way to run code fetched later.

f_csp_remote.message: The policy now allows scripts from other servers

f_csp_remote_why.message: Scripts loaded from a server can change at any time, without a store update.

f_update_url_changed_why.message: From {1} to {2}. An extension that updates from its own server skips store review.

f_homepage_changed_why.message: From {1} to {2}. Sometimes a sign the extension changed hands.

f_author_changed_why.message: From {1} to {2}. Sometimes a sign the extension was sold.

f_externally_connectable.message: Websites or apps can now message it: {1}

f_externally_connectable_why.message: The listed sites or extensions can send it messages directly.

f_dnr_header_why.message: New network rules remove or replace headers such as Content-Security-Policy, which protect pages from injected code. QuickLens did this in February 2026.

f_sites_new_why.message: The scripts now name sites they did not name before. Check that they belong to the developer or to services the extension uses.

f_sites_new_data_why.message: They appear in files that list many sites, such as filter lists, so they add no points.

f_remote_combo.message: New sites plus code that runs text or injects scripts

f_remote_combo_why.message: Together, these are the usual shape of “download code later, then run it”.

f_obfuscated_new_why.message: Code written to be hard to read: hex names, escaped strings or long encoded blobs. Chrome Web Store policy does not allow obfuscated code.

f_wasm_new_why.message: WebAssembly is compiled code and is hard to inspect.

f_minified_new_why.message: Compressed but ordinary code; listed for completeness.

pattern_function_constructor_why.message: Builds a function out of a string; the same risk as eval.

pattern_string_timer_why.message: Runs a string as code after a delay.

pattern_document_write_why.message: Writes raw HTML, scripts included, into a page.

pattern_script_element_why.message: Can add scripts to a page, possibly from another server.

pattern_remote_import_scripts_why.message: Loads a script from a server into a worker.

pattern_remote_dynamic_import_why.message: Loads a JavaScript module from a server.

pattern_execute_script_why.message: Injects scripts into your tabs. Common, but new in this extension.

pattern_execute_script_code_why.message: Injects text into your tabs as code.

pattern_dynamic_header_rules.message: rules that edit security headers while running

pattern_dynamic_header_rules_why.message: The code adds network rules at run time and names headers such as Content-Security-Policy.

pattern_websocket_why.message: Opens a long-lived connection to a server.

opt_autoDisable.message: Turn off an extension when its update is high risk

opt_autoDisable_help.message: crxdiff switches it off and tells you; one click turns it back on. Extensions installed by policy cannot be turned off.

opt_notify.message: Notify me about updates worth a look

opt_interval_help.message: crxdiff also checks as soon as Chrome reports that an extension was updated.

opt_ignore_help.message: Ticked extensions are not downloaded or compared.

opt_export_help.message: One file with what crxdiff keeps for each extension: manifest, file hashes and sizes, sites and patterns. No source code.

opt_reset_confirm.message: Delete all baselines and reports? New baselines are taken on the next check.

opt_privacy.message: crxdiff connects only to Google’s update servers (clients2.google.com and clients2.googleusercontent.com), and only to download extensions you already have. No account, no analytics, no telemetry.
